text: For unfair treatment such as illegal fees or rejected transactions, the March 2026 Zambanker describes a three-step Path to Justice. The first step is to complain to the financial service provider at its branch or customer-care level.
section_or_page: Printed p.12, “BoZ Declares Consumer Protection Central to Stability Mandate,” Path to Justice, step 1
review_note: Corrected page reference to printed p.12; narrowed to source examples and first step.
original_text: If you face unfair treatment, illegal fees, or rejected transactions by a financial institution, you should follow the official three-step Path to Justice: first, lodge a formal complaint directly with the specific Financial Service Provider (FSP) at the branch or customer care level.

text: If a complaint is unresolved at the branch or customer-care level, the next step in the Path to Justice is to escalate it to the financial service provider's head-office complaints unit.
section_or_page: Printed p.12, same article, Path to Justice, step 2
review_note: Corrected page reference to printed p.12; preserves the second step.
original_text: As the second step in resolving a banking dispute, if your complaint is not resolved satisfactorily at the branch level, you must escalate the matter to the Financial Service Provider's head-office complaints unit.

text: If all internal complaint options with a financial service provider are exhausted, the article says consumers can contact the Bank of Zambia through its official channels for case review.
section_or_page: Printed p.12, same article, Path to Justice, step 3
review_note: Corrected page reference to printed p.12; directs to BoZ only after internal FSP options are exhausted.
original_text: As the final step in the Path to Justice, if all internal complaint options with your financial service provider are exhausted without resolution, you can contact the Bank of Zambia to independently review your case.

text: The Bank of Zambia's Contact Us webpage provides a general enquiry form, telephone contacts and email contact details.
section_or_page: Contact Us webpage; general enquiry form and contact section
review_note: General Contact Us details only; not identified as the formal complaint-submission route.
original_text: The Bank of Zambia provides official communication channels including telephone, email, and in-person visits at its Head Office and regional offices for consumers to submit formal escalated complaints.

text: The March 2026 Zambanker describes market-conduct supervision as ensuring that financial service providers operate fairly.
section_or_page: Printed p.12, Strategic Plan priorities, market-conduct supervision bullet
original_text: The Bank of Zambia's market-conduct supervision ensures that Financial Service Providers operate fairly, transparently, and adhere to strict consumer protection standards across all banking products.

text: The March 2026 Zambanker article describes a safe financial product as secure, transparent and fair.
review_note: Removed unsupported “fully transparent in pricing and terms”; not presented as a legal definition.
original_text: A safe financial product, as defined under Bank of Zambia consumer protection standards, is one that is secure, fully transparent in pricing and terms, and fair to everyday consumers.

text: The March 2026 Zambanker says Electronic Funds Transfers (EFTs) are used for a wide range of transactions and routine commercial transfers, and are processed in batches through the Direct Debit and Credit Clearing (DDACC) system.
section_or_page: Printed p.7, “What Are the Alternatives to Cheques?”, EFT paragraph
review_note: Corrected source from SRC004 to SRC002 printed p.7; kept supported batch/DDACC information.
original_text: Electronic Funds Transfers (EFTs) are processed in batches through the Direct Debit and Credit Clearing (DDACC) system for routine commercial transfers, salaries, and bill payments.

text: The March 2026 Zambanker says Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) is designed for high-value and time-critical payments and supports transaction values from micro-payments starting at 1 ngwee to very large-value transactions.
review_note: Corrected source from SRC004 to SRC002 printed p.7; removed unsupported “designed by BoZ.”
original_text: Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) is designed by the Bank of Zambia for high-value and time-critical payments, supporting transaction values starting from 1 ngwee up to very large corporate transfers.

text: The FinScope 2025 survey reports that adult uptake of mobile money increased to 76.1 percent in 2025 from 58.4 percent in 2020.
section_or_page: Printed p.9, “Uptake of Formal Financial Services”
review_note: Removed unsupported interoperability/infrastructure claim; reclassified to financial_education survey finding.
original_text: Mobile money remains the primary driver of financial inclusion in Zambia, enabling interoperable digital transactions across different platforms and institutions via the national payment infrastructure.

text: The Bank of Zambia says it supervises and regulates commercial banks and that commercial banks are licensed under the Banking and Financial Services Act.
section_or_page: Bank Financial Institutions webpage, opening mandate and licensing paragraphs
review_note: Changed attribution from directory SRC007 to official BoZ page SRC010; narrowed to commercial-bank supervision/licensing.
original_text: The Bank of Zambia regulates commercial banks and authorized financial service institutions registered under the Banking and Financial Services Act to maintain financial stability.

text: The Bank of Zambia's Registered Financial Institutions directory lists institutions and licence categories. Consumers can consult the live directory to check the institution name and the category shown by the regulator.
section_or_page: Registered Financial Institutions live directory, institution and licence-category table
review_note: Live directory lookup only; no implication that listing guarantees safety.
original_text: Consumers can verify whether a financial institution or commercial bank is officially authorized by checking the official Bank of Zambia registered institutions directory on the official website.

text: The March 2026 Zambanker reports that the Ministry of Finance and National Planning, the Bank of Zambia and the Bankers Association of Zambia launched 2026 Financial Literacy Week with a call for year-round financial education.
section_or_page: Printed p.10, “2026 Financial Literacy Week Launched with Call for Year-Round Engagement”
review_note: Limited to the 2026 Financial Literacy Week launch and year-round focus.
original_text: The Bank of Zambia, in partnership with the Ministry of Finance and National Planning and the Bankers Association of Zambia, promotes continuous year-round financial literacy to educate the public.

text: A Bank of Zambia public notice dated 13 August 2025 says the Bank developed and released an educational app called “Zambian Banknotes” with information and interactive visuals about security features of the new currency.
source_title: Public Notice: Launch of the K100 and K50 Banknotes and Release of an Educational App on the New Currency
section_or_page: One-page Public Notice, manually inspected; app purpose and description
review_note: Visually checked one-page notice; corrected page reference and avoided current app-store claims.
original_text: The Bank of Zambia released an official educational mobile application alongside the K100 and K50 banknotes to help members of the public easily identify currency security features.

text: FinScope 2025 reports overall financial inclusion rose to 80.1 percent in 2025 from 69.4 percent in 2020. The report says the increase was supported by improved uptake of both formal and informal financial services.
section_or_page: FinScope report overview, printed p.1, and financial inclusion metrics, printed p.6
review_note: Separated overall inclusion from formal inclusion/mobile-money figures.
original_text: According to the FinScope 2025 Survey published by the Bank of Zambia, overall financial inclusion in Zambia rose to 80.1 percent, driven largely by the expansion of mobile money services.

text: The Bank of Zambia Contact Us page lists its Head Office at Bank Square, Cairo Road, P.O. Box 30080, Lusaka, and gives the telephone number (+260) 211 399 300 and email info@boz.zm.
section_or_page: Contact Us webpage, Head Office section
review_note: Verified current Head Office details; no formal complaint claim.
original_text: The Bank of Zambia Head Office is located at Bank Square, Cairo Road, P.O. Box 30080, Lusaka, Zambia, with official telephone contact (+260) 211 399 300 and email info@boz.zm.

text: The Bank of Zambia Contact Us page lists its Regional Office at Buteko Avenue, P.O. Box 71511, Ndola, and gives the telephone number (+260) 212 399 600.
section_or_page: Contact Us webpage, Regional Office section
original_text: The Bank of Zambia Regional Office is located at Buteko Avenue, P.O. Box 71511, Ndola, Zambia, with official telephone contact (+260) 212 399 600.

text: The March 2026 Zambanker says the Bank of Zambia 2024–2027 Strategic Plan prioritises cyber-security resilience, market-conduct supervision and improved dispute resolution.
review_note: Corrected page to p.12; removed implied outcome guarantee.
original_text: The Bank of Zambia's strategic plan prioritizes cyber security resilience, market-conduct supervision, and improved dispute resolution to protect financial consumers across Zambia.

text: The Bank of Zambia's payment-systems oversight includes mobile-money payments. It says payment-system rules aim to inform consumers about their rights and obligations when using those systems.
section_or_page: Payment System Oversight, paragraph on Widely Important Payment Systems; “Consumer Protection and Competition Law” subsection
review_note: Narrow overview of BoZ oversight and consumer rights/obligations. Does not supply transaction instructions, fee details, failed-payment remedies or complaint timelines.
original_text: NEW CANDIDATE — identified during the official BoZ mobile-money coverage recheck; no original KB passage.
